newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: New Yugo finmin says creditors must become active.
newsitem.headline: New Yugo finmin says creditors must become active.

text.p: Bozidar Gazivoda, Yugoslavia's new finance minister, said Belgrade wanted to repay its external debt but urged creditors to be more active in seeking a rescheduling deal.
"Yugoslavia will repay its external debt," Gazivoda said but added that solutions had to be sought together with all creditors.

"Yugoslavia will seek a grace period in debt servicing as well as a debt reduction. But creditors must also become more active in seeking ways to be paid off. They know we can't pay back at once," Gazivoda said.
He insisted that Yugoslavia first needed funds to kick-start its economy and make it able to pay back debts.

According to unofficial estimates, Yugoslavia's external debt runs around $9 billion, while the country's forex reserves are seen standing between $220 million and $270 million. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
